alt.en: A black-and-white photograph of a tall, square brick bell tower with arched openings at the top and a clock on each face, beside a brick church with a broad hipped roof, seen behind bare winter trees and telegraph poles; part of another brick building shows at the lower left.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro de un alto campanario de ladrillo, cuadrado, con aberturas en arco en lo alto y un reloj en cada cara, junto a una iglesia de ladrillo con un amplio tejado a cuatro aguas, vistos tras árboles de invierno sin hojas y postes de telégrafo; abajo a la izquierda se ve parte de otro edificio de ladrillo.

caption.en: The Memorial Church at Hampton Institute in Virginia, photographed about 1902; seven years later the Institute Press at Hampton printed this song with the verses we sing.
caption.es: La Memorial Church del Hampton Institute, en Virginia, fotografiada hacia 1902; siete años después, la imprenta del instituto en Hampton imprimió esta canción con las estrofas que cantamos.

source: Virginia Hall, Hampton Institute, Va. (glass negative, 8 x 10 in., right section; the negative's own caption: "014186. Memorial Church and Academic Hall, Hampton Institute, Va."), William Henry Jackson, photographer, Detroit Publishing Co., copyright 1902. Cropped to the church and tower.
library: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
licenceEvidence: Library of Congress record LCCN 2016800885, field 540: "No known restrictions on publication." (record read through LoC's SRU server; see rights.md). Photograph copyright 1902; Jackson died 1942.
credit: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, Detroit Publishing Company Collection, LC-D4-10628

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "I Will Pray." in black-letter type and marked "Infervorato.": a refrain for four voices on two staves in E-flat and 4/4, "Ev'ry time I feel the Spirit Moving in my heart, I will pray.", then a part marked "Solo." with three verses, "When you hear me pray, my Jesus", over two staves of hummed chords marked "(Hum.)"; page number 4 at the foot.
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el encabezado "I Will Pray." en letra gótica y la indicación "Infervorato.": un estribillo a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas, en Mi bemol y 4/4, "Ev'ry time I feel the Spirit Moving in my heart, I will pray.", y luego una parte marcada "Solo." con tres estrofas, "When you hear me pray, my Jesus", sobre dos pentagramas de acordes tarareados marcados "(Hum.)"; al pie, el número de página 4.

caption.en: "I Will Pray", page 4 of Folk Songs of the American Negro, Number Two (Nashville, 1907), edited by Frederick J. Work at Fisk University: the earliest known printing of this song, with its refrain and three other verses sung alone over humming.
caption.es: "I Will Pray", en la página 4 de Folk Songs of the American Negro, Number Two (Nashville, 1907), editado por Frederick J. Work en la Universidad Fisk: la primera impresión conocida de esta canción, con su estribillo y otras tres estrofas cantadas por una sola voz sobre un tarareo.

source: Frederick J. Work, ed., Folk Songs of the American Negro, Number Two, introduction by John W. Work (Nashville: Work Bros. & Hart Co., [1907]), "I Will Pray", p. 4
library: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, University Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published Nashville 1907; editor Frederick J. Work died 1942, John W. Work died 1925; words and tune traditional. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, University Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: Part of a printed page of music headed "Ev'ry Time I Feel the Spirit" in black-letter type: a refrain for four voices on two staves in E-flat and 4/4, "Ev'ry time I feel the Spirit moving in my heart I will pray.", marked "Fine.", then one line of tune with three verses under it, "Up-on the mountain my Lord spoke", over an empty lower staff of rests, marked "D. C.".
alt.es: Parte de una página impresa de música con el encabezado "Ev'ry Time I Feel the Spirit" en letra gótica: un estribillo a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas, en Mi bemol y 4/4, "Ev'ry time I feel the Spirit moving in my heart I will pray.", con la indicación "Fine.", y luego una sola línea de melodía con tres estrofas debajo, "Up-on the mountain my Lord spoke", sobre un pentagrama inferior vacío, solo con silencios, con la indicación "D. C.".

caption.en: Page 169 of Hampton Institute's 1909 edition of Religious Folk Songs of the Negro: the refrain in four parts, then the mountain, shining and Jordan verses as one line of tune for one voice; we sing the first two.
caption.es: La página 169 de la edición de 1909 de Religious Folk Songs of the Negro, del Hampton Institute: el estribillo a cuatro voces y luego las estrofas de la montaña, del brillo y del Jordán como una sola línea de melodía para una voz; cantamos las dos primeras.

source: Religious Folk Songs of the Negro as Sung on the Plantations, new edition, arranged by the musical directors of the Hampton Normal and Agricultural Institute from the original edition by Thomas P. Fenner (Hampton, Va.: The Institute Press, 1909), "Ev'ry Time I Feel the Spirit", p. 169. Cropped to this song (the end of the song before it is cut away).

callNumber: M1670 .H3 R4; OCLC 977588305; Internet Archive religiousfolkson00hamp
licenceEvidence: Published Hampton, Va., 1909, its arrangers unnamed ("the musical directors"); Thomas P. Fenner died 1912; words and tune traditional. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).

alt.es: La parte superior de una página impresa de música, la 169, con los encabezados "Hymns of Meditation" y "Ev'ry Time I Feel the Spirit" y la indicación "Andante molto espress.", negra igual a 68 a 72: un estribillo marcado "Tutti" a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas, en Mi bemol y 4/4, y luego una línea marcada "Solo" con tres estrofas debajo, "Up-on the moun-tain my Lord spoke", sobre un pentagrama inferior vacío, con la indicación "D. caption.en: Page 169 of R. Nathaniel Dett's Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (1927), which prints the 1909 setting again with "Tutti" for the refrain and "Solo" for the verses: the page our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: La página 169 de Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (1927), de R. Nathaniel Dett, que vuelve a imprimir la armonización de 1909 con "Tutti" para el estribillo y "Solo" para las estrofas: la página de la que está tomado nuestro arreglo.

source: R. Nathaniel Dett, ed., Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (Hampton, Va.: Hampton Institute Press, 1927), "Hymns of Meditation", "Ev'ry Time I Feel the Spirit", p. 169. Cropped to this song (the next song on the page is cut away).
